Thanks — quick operational notes so the bundle is explicit for the assessor: 

1) PR gating / approvals
- Branch protection enforced on 'main' and release branches via GitHub. Required status checks: unit tests, lint, and the Redwood quality gate (policy-runner).
- We will include: branch-protection screenshot, an example rejected PR (automated policy block), and an exported PR event snippet (last 30 days).

2) CI identity & credentialing
- CI platforms: GitHub Actions (primary) + internal runner fleet. We use OIDC for short-lived tokens issued to GitHub Actions workflows that assume a Redwood service account (AWS STS / GCP workload identity).
- Onboarding: developer requests service-account via internal portal -> approval workflow -> least-priv role assigned for runtime.
- Rotation: OIDC tokens are short-lived by design; long-lived credentials are never checked into CI. We will include the OIDC trust policy and a sample workflow snippet showing the assume-role flow.

3) Secrets & vaulting
- HashiCorp Vault is used for CI secrets; CI jobs fetch secrets at runtime with RBAC enforced. We rotate secrets with an automated job; we'll include a rotation log extract (CSV) showing timestamps and actors for the last 90 days.

Grace will drop the artifacts; I'll prepare a brief README explaining the artifacts and point to the exact SIG question mappings.

Attachment: ci-access-matrix.csv (will be attached by Grace)

Jonas Weber
Director, Inference Platform Ops

Hi Maya / team — attaching the requested artifacts below (stubs attached here for the assessor):

Attachments included:
- ci-access-matrix.csv — lists service accounts used by CI, least-priv roles, owner, created_at
- pr-gate-policy.md — text export of the policy-runner rules and branch-protection config
- code-review-sample.patch — small PR showing automated policy failure + reviewer approval trail
- secrets-handling-procedure.pdf — internal procedure for secret creation, access, ephemeral fetch pattern, and emergency rotation steps

Highlights / notes:
- The CI jobs use OIDC tokens with a maximum lifetime of 5 minutes for ephemeral workflows. No long-lived secrets in repo.
- Vault paths are namespaced per-team; CI uses short TTL renewals and token wrapping for privileged fetches.
- Rotation job (cron) rotates application-level API keys every 30 days; user-facing tokens follow a 90-day cadence. Rotation logs include agent and change reason.
